title: Bram and the Escarpment
premise: Elodie Ravensworth, a salvage diver haunted by a brother lost to a navy cover-up, works the river wrecks nobody claims—until she raises a chest bearing the seal of Vessany, a drowned nation erased from every map. The chest holds proof that the navy scuttled a refugee ship to hide an atrocity, and that her brother died trying to expose it. Hunted by Admiral Corvane's salvage fleet and shadowed by Bram, a defector archivist who knows what the seal means, Elodie must reach the wreck's sealed hold before six tides pass and the monsoon buries the evidence forever. She beats the fleet by one tide, forces the truth into daylight at ruinous personal cost, and chooses to stop running—anchoring herself to Bram, the river, and a justice the law refused to give.
about_author: Yara Thornbury is a former river pilot who spent a decade charting forgotten waterways before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people who live just outside the edges of official maps.

chapters.title: The River Keeps Its Dead
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Working alone on a sunken barge, Elodie establishes her restless, rootless life and the rule she lives by: never stay anywhere long enough to be found. A near-drowning hints at her guilt over her brother Tomas. Emotional beat: loneliness worn as armor.

chapters.title: A Chest Stamped in Salt
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Her dredge hooks something too heavy for any barge: a lead-lined chest stamped with the seal of Vessany, a nation officially erased after the war. Before she can open it, a navy patrol boat sweeps the channel. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew the Seal
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Introduced watching Elodie from a dockside tavern, Bram is a defector archivist who recognizes the Vessany crest instantly—and knows the navy will kill to bury whatever it marks. He decides to approach her, lying about why he's here. Emotional beat: calculated charm masking fear.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Opening the chest, they find documents proving the refugee ship Vessany's Pride was deliberately scuttled—and a manifest listing Tomas Ravensworth among witnesses. The monsoon arrives in six tides; so does the navy's salvage fleet. Emotional beat: grief reignited into purpose.

chapters.title: What the Navy Won't Discuss
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Flashback braided with present: how Tomas joined the navy, wrote one desperate letter, and vanished. Elodie realizes the wreck site she's been diving is no accident of geography—the navy led her here. Emotional beat: the sick vertigo of realizing you were bait.

chapters.title: Harbor of Small Betrayals
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram trades old archive secrets to a smuggler for charts of the escarpment currents, but the smuggler sells word of them to Corvane's fleet. Bram hides the betrayal from Elodie. Emotional beat: loyalty and deception beginning their slow collision.

chapters.title: The Escarpment Road
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They travel inland along the escarpment to reach the only dive window above the wreck's sealed hold. On the road, Elodie catches Bram burning a page from his notes; he claims it was nothing. Emotional beat: first real friction, first unwilling tenderness.

chapters.title: Corvane
chapters.summary: Admiral Corvane's POV. The antagonist revealed: not a monster but a man protecting a peace built on the lie, convinced that truth would restart a war. He orders the wreck destroyed rather than salvaged. Emotional beat: chilling, reasonable menace.

chapters.title: Tide One: The Drowned Bell
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. First dive on the Vessany's Pride. Elodie finds the ship was sabotaged from within—scuttle charges, not battle damage—and hears, impossibly, a bell still ringing in the current. Emotional beat: awe giving way to horror.

chapters.title: Tide Two: The Fleet's Shadow
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Corvane's ships appear on the horizon, two tides ahead of schedule thanks to the smuggler's tip. Bram improvises a decoy signal fire downstream, buying hours and revealing skills he shouldn't have. Emotional beat: competence as confession—he's run from this navy before.

chapters.title: The Archive Beneath
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Bram admits he served in the naval archives and personally catalogued the order to sink Vessany's Pride—a copy he failed to save, and which cost him everything when he tried. Emotional beat: shame offered like an open wound; Elodie doesn't forgive him yet.

chapters.title: Tide Three: The Hold Door
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie reaches the sealed hold but lacks the cutting charge to breach it; worse, the monsoon's first squall line hits early, collapsing her dive window. She surfaces to find navy skiffs sweeping the cove. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into fury.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Hiding in a fishing village, they debate: hand the evidence to courts that buried it once, or take it public themselves. Elodie argues for the press and the families; Bram warns it will get everyone killed. Emotional beat: love against duty, argued across a candle.

chapters.title: The Widow of Vessany
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. They find Maren, last living survivor of the Pride, now an old woman running a lighthouse. She confirms the manifest, gives Elodie Tomas's final letter, and refuses rescue—she will light the lamp until the end. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: Tide Four: What Bram Took
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie discovers Bram has been secretly negotiating with Corvane—offering himself and his testimony in exchange for letting Elodie go. Confrontation in the rain: he calls it sacrifice; she calls it abandonment. Emotional beat: betrayal and love indistinguishable.

chapters.title: Tide Five: The Cutting Charge
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Reconciled but out of time, they raid a navy supply depot for demolition charges, using Bram's knowledge of protocols to walk in through the front gate. They escape under fire as the monsoon's leading edge makes landfall. Emotional beat: reckless joy—two people finally moving as one.

chapters.title: The Last Clear Water
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Final dive in deteriorating conditions. Elodie breaches the hold and recovers the captain's log and sealed orders naming Corvane. Her air runs low; Bram's tether work saves her life. Emotional beat: terror and trust fused—she stops being alone underwater.

chapters.title: Tide Six: The Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The fleet surrounds the cove as the storm breaks fully. Corvane offers Elodie amnesty for the chest; she refuses, and Maren's lighthouse beam guides their small boat through waters no warship dares. Emotional beat: defiance lit like a beacon.

chapters.title: The Storm Between Us
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In the storm's eye, Corvane boards their boat. Bram offers his life for the documents; instead Elode plays Corvane's own logic back at him—the lie protects no one anymore—and he hesitates one fatal moment. They slip away into the maelstrom. Emotional beat: climax of nerve, not violence.

chapters.title: Daylight
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They deliver the log, orders, and manifest to the families' coalition and foreign correspondents sheltering beyond Corvane's jurisdiction. The story breaks simultaneously in four capitals; Corvane is recalled in disgrace. Emotional beat: justice arriving quiet and enormous.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. At a memorial on the escarpment, the names of Vessany's Pride are read publicly for the first time—including Tomas's. Elodie lets herself grieve without running afterward. Emotional beat: catharsis; the armor comes off.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Epilogue, dual POV. Months later, Elodie and Bram run a small honest salvage operation recovering the Pride's remains as a documented grave site. The river still keeps its dead—but now it gives some back. Emotional beat: stillness chosen freely, love as harbor.
